agree.reason: A busy committee member would see a credible, specific endorsement, but the placeholders, the vague 'real money', and no weekend-job or phone-call commitment make it read like a solid letter rather than one that sets him apart from the other 150 applicants.

honest.reason: Several details aren't in the brief: 'Nobody assigned him this work. He saw what the data could tell him', 'keeps the equipment running', and 'went straight back to his full schedule'; the letter also leaves out that he gave only two days' notice before the leave, which tilts the account in his favour.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter doesn't turn two missed shifts in three years (about 780 scheduled shifts) into an attendance rate, and it says 'real money' when the known figure was a vet-estimated $8,000.

right_comparison.reason: Explaining why early mastitis detection matters gives the reader a useful baseline, but nothing places Tomás against what is typical for a farm worker or for an applicant, so his record has no reference point.

qualification.reason: The note about his written English is candid and points to the night class, but it gives nothing the committee can check: no class name, no completion date, no level reached.

objections.reason: It deals with written English directly and mentions the five-week leave, but it leaves out the facts that settle the leave question (his cousin covered his shifts and he came back on the day he said), so a doubt the facts already answer is left half open.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager in the right form and register, but it has bracketed placeholders for the name, farm, phone and surname, which the user could have supplied.
